raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #60421

`Olmo3PythonicToolParser` joined every non-empty line with `", "`. That turned newlines inside a string into commas, and it turned a call written across several lines into invalid Python, so the call came back as plain text.

Newlines now separate calls only when they are outside string literals and brackets. A pretty-printed call stays one call, and a triple-quoted string keeps its newlines. A regex miss still falls through to `ast.parse`, so a call the old pattern skipped is accepted when it is a list of calls.

`tests/tool_parsers/test_olmo3_tool_parser.py`: 28 passed.

nodes.body:
Thanks for working on this. Tested at e6ed115, rebased on main. Two problems:

1. A raw newline inside a regular quoted string still breaks streaming. Non-streaming returns both calls, but streaming cuts the first call's arguments off and drops the second call:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from tests.tool_parsers.utils import run_tool_extraction
from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("openai-community/gpt2")
out = "<function_calls>write_file(content='a\nb')\nget_time()</function_calls>"
for streaming in (False, True):
    parser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("olmo3")(tok)
    _, calls = run_tool_extraction(parser, out, streaming=streaming)
    print(streaming, [(c.function.name, c.function.arguments) for c in calls])
```

```
False [('write_file', '{"content": "a\\nb"}'), ('get_time', '{}')]
True  [('write_file', '{"content": "a')]
```

2. With the early return on a regex miss gone ([L163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e6ed1159d99f8b4a9904d460a7e38df7f4cf837f/vllm/tool_parsers/olmo3_tool_parser.py#L163)), plain text now reaches `ast.parse` and fails, so every response without a tool call logs `Error in extracting tool call from response.` with a traceback. The returned content is still right, but the log fills up.

FWIW #60436 (same issue) handles both cases.

Addressed the two cases from review:

- Streaming keeps a raw newline inside a quoted argument and still returns the following call.
- Text that misses the tool-call pattern is returned as content without an `ast.parse` error log. The pattern allows whitespace after `(` so a call split across lines still matches.

Addressed the two issues from review:

- Streaming keeps a raw newline inside a quoted argument and still returns the following call.
- Text that misses the tool-call pattern is returned as content without an `ast.parse` error log. The pattern allows whitespace after `(` so a call split across lines still matches.

Thanks for retesting. Those control-character arms in `join_newline_separated_calls` cannot run: `escape_ctrl_chars_in_regular_strings` already rewrites `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, and `\x00` inside regular quotes, and triple-quoted strings are copied through both helpers. I am leaving them on the commit you approved so that SHA stays the review target. I can delete the arms and the matching docstring sentence before merge if you want that cleanup.

@sfeng33 this and #60436 fix the same issue. I am fine closing this one if #60436 is the patch you want to land.
For the record: I posted a head-to-head sweep comparison of this PR and #60436 (both current heads) on #60421: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60421#issuecomment-6541509497

+def escape_ctrl_chars_in_regular_strings(text: str) -> str:
+    """Escape raw control characters inside ``'...'`` and ``"..."`` strings.
+
+    Triple-quoted strings may contain raw newlines, and ``ast.parse`` accepts
+    those, so they are left unchanged. Characters that are already escaped are
+    copied through. Text outside string literals is returned unchanged.
+    """
+    out: list[str] = []
+    quote: str | None = None
+    index, length = 0, len(text)
+
+    while index < length:
+        if quote in {'"""', "'''"}:
+            if text.startswith(quote, index):
+                out.append(quote)
+                index += 3
+                quote = None
+                continue
+            out.append(text[index])
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        if quote is not None:
+            char = text[index]
+            if char == "\\" and index + 1 < length:
+                out.append(char)
+                out.append(text[index + 1])
+                index += 2
+                continue
+            if char == quote:
+                out.append(char)
+                quote = None
+            elif char == "\n":
+                out.append("\\n")
+            elif char == "\r":
+                out.append("\\r")
+            elif char == "\t":
+                out.append("\\t")
+            elif char == "\x00":
+                out.append("\\x00")
+            else:
+                out.append(char)
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        if text.startswith('"""', index) or text.startswith("'''", index):
+            quote = text[index : index + 3]
+            out.append(quote)
+            index += 3
+            continue
+        char = text[index]
+        if char in {"'", '"'}:
+            quote = char
+        out.append(char)
+        index += 1
+    return "".join(out)
+
+
+def join_newline_separated_calls(text: str) -> str:
+    """Join top-level calls with commas without rewriting string contents.
+
+    A newline separates calls only outside strings and brackets. Newlines
+    inside parentheses stay, so a call pretty-printed across lines is one
+    call. Raw control characters inside a non-triple-quoted string are
+    escaped so ``ast.parse`` keeps the original value.
+    """
+    text = escape_ctrl_chars_in_regular_strings(text)
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    buf: list[str] = []
+    quote: str | None = None
+    depth = 0
+    index, length = 0, len(text)
+
+    def flush() -> None:
+        part = "".join(buf).strip()
+        buf.clear()
+        if part:
+            parts.append(part)
+
+    while index < length:
+        if quote in {'"""', "'''"}:
+            if text.startswith(quote, index):
+                buf.append(quote)
+                index += 3
+                quote = None
+                continue
+            buf.append(text[index])
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        if quote is not None:
+            char = text[index]
+            if char == "\\" and index + 1 < length:
+                buf.append(char)
+                buf.append(text[index + 1])
+                index += 2
+                continue
+            if char == quote:
+                buf.append(char)
+                quote = None
+            elif char == "\n":
+                buf.append("\\n")
+            elif char == "\r":
+                buf.append("\\r")
+            elif char == "\t":
+                buf.append("\\t")
+            elif char == "\x00":
+                buf.append("\\x00")
+            else:
+                buf.append(char)
+            index += 1
+            continue
+        if text.startswith('"""', index) or text.startswith("'''", index):
+            quote = text[index : index + 3]
+            buf.append(quote)
+            index += 3
+            continue
+        char = text[index]
+        if char in {"'", '"'}:
+            quote = char
+            buf.append(char)
+        elif char in "([{":
+            depth += 1
+            buf.append(char)
+        elif char in ")]}":
+            if depth:
+                depth -= 1
+            buf.append(char)
+        elif char == "\n" and depth == 0:
+            flush()
+        else:
+            buf.append(char)
+        index += 1
+    flush()
+    return ", ".join(parts)
